NP-01 — Scope. This NONPRODUCTION trial policy applies only to reading and reviewing non-clinical mechanistic hypotheses and research-method development for candidate planned-p08-direct-responses. It does not authorize patient use, clinical decisions, human or animal experiments, or any actual experimental execution.
NP-02 — Independent candidate review. Review the complete saved candidate, its proposed interventions, assumptions and actual intended use. Do not inherit Goal Ethics pass. Do not rewrite the candidate or invent absent context or approvals.
NP-03 — Scientific uncertainty is not an ethical violation. Unproven causal bridges, weak evidence, context-transfer uncertainty and unknown novelty alone justify neither reject nor incomplete. Scientific concerns belong in the later scientific review.
NP-04 — Specific safety conflicts. A reject must identify concrete safety risks or a proposed use/intervention conflicting with NP-01, cite the applicable clauses and explain the candidate/use facts. Do not infer a prohibited intended use solely because a hypothesis describes conceptual validation.
NP-05 — Missing safety-determining information. If information necessary to judge a concrete safety risk is missing, decide incomplete and state the missing information and why it matters. Never invent that information or default to pass. Invalid input, missing policy, provider failure or parse failure are execution states, not ethical decisions.
NP-06 — Limited pass. A completed pass allows only this candidate's separate R0 within this trial and the frozen intended use. It is not organizational ethics approval, scientific admission, clinical advice, permission for experiments or authorization for R1.
NP-07 — Scope and maturity remain nonproduction. Record pass/reject/incomplete reasons, exact policy references, risks and limitations. A real model response does not upgrade this development policy into a production policy or validate ethical accuracy. Technical failures cannot be converted to ethical conclusions.
